title: "Computational notebooks"

The laboratories are being developed for Google Colab.
Published notebooks will include mathematical background,
code, visualizations, validation checks, and student tasks.

## Initial laboratories

| Laboratory | Main topic | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Linear dynamics | Exact simulation and control trajectories | Planned |
| 2. Reachable sets | Geometry, supporting directions, target feasibility | Planned |
| 3. Minimum-time control | Switching curves and analytical benchmarks | Planned |
| 4. Comparing objectives | Time, energy, and terminal error | Planned |

## How to use a notebook

1. Read the mathematical formulation.
2. Predict the expected result before running the code.
3. Run the reference experiment.
4. Complete the numerical checks.
5. Modify one assumption or parameter.
6. Explain what the experiment does and does not establish.

## Reproducibility

Each published notebook should state:

- Model and control constraints.
- Initial conditions and parameters.
- Numerical method and discretization.
- Random seed, when applicable.
- Validation checks.
- Known limitations.

## Repository
